title: Iron-fortified oat cereal with pear
summary: Creamy infant oat cereal stirred with soft pear: an easy way to get iron into the first months of solids.
texture: Smooth and runny at first, like a thick soup. Make it thicker over the following weeks by adding less liquid.
ingredients: 1 small ripe pear, peeled, cored and chopped
3 to 4 tbsp breast milk or prepared infant formula
steps: Steam the pear for 5 to 8 minutes until very soft, then mash or blend until smooth.
In a small bowl, stir the infant cereal with the breast milk or formula until smooth.
Stir in 1 to 2 tablespoons of the pear puree. Adjust with more liquid for a runnier texture.
Serve right away: infant cereal thickens as it sits.
choking: Use infant cereal (it dissolves smoothly), not regular rolled oats, at this stage.
Cook the pear until it mashes with no hard pieces.
storage: Make the cereal fresh each time. Pear puree keeps 2 days in the fridge or 1 month frozen in an ice-cube tray.
tips: Babies' iron stores start running low around 6 months, so iron-fortified cereals, lentils, meat and fish are great early foods.
Oat cereal is a good everyday choice: it's lower in arsenic than rice cereal.
